# faraday_atlas (Resource)



## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "faraday_atlas" "stores" {
  name = "stores"
  options = {
    hosted_csv = {
      upload_directory = "stores"
    }
  }
  output_to_locations = {
    name                    = "store_name"
    reference_key           = "store_id"
    house_number_and_street = ["street"]
    city                    = "city"
    state                   = "state"
    postcode                = "postcode"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) An identifying name for this atlas.
- `options` (Attributes) Atlas connection options (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--options))
- `output_to_locations` (Attributes) How to build a location out of each row of the source data. Each member below names a column in the source data. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--output_to_locations))

### Optional

- `connection_id` (String) The UUID of a connection - see <a href="https://faraday.ai/developers/reference/createconnection">/connections</a> for more detail. Only a subset of connection types can be configured for atlas ingestion - see the list available in `options`. If this is null, the account's hosted CSV connection is used, and is provisioned if it does not exist yet.

### Read-Only

- `archived_at` (String) If not null, this resource will no longer receive updates, but will still be visable.
- `counts` (Attributes) Location counts for this atlas. These will only be displayed if the atlas built successfully. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--counts))
- `created_at` (String) When this resource was created.
- `detected_columns` (Attributes List) An array of columns (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detected_columns))
- `id` (String) A unique ID for this resource.
- `last_read_input_at` (String) The last time this resource's input was read.
- `last_updated_config_at` (String) The last time this resource's configuration was updated. If this is more recent than last_updated_output_at, the resource will be rebuilt.
- `last_updated_output_at` (String) The last time this resource successfully built.
- `resource_type` (String) The type of this resource.
- `status` (String) The current state of this resource and any updates.
- `status_changed_at` (String) When the status of this resource was last updated.
- `status_error` (String) If this resource has `status == "error"`, this will contain an error message.
- `updated_at` (String) When this resource was last updated.

<a id="nestedatt--options--gcp_gcs_csv"></a>
### Nested Schema for `options.gcp_gcs_csv`

Required:

- `prefix` (String) The prefix inside the bucket. May optionally include full filename, file globs (not regexp), and stftime date parsing formatting (which will override blob storage's native timestamps). For example, orders/, orders/file.csv, orders/*.csv, or orders/files-%Y-%m-%d.csv

Optional:

- `delimiter` (String) Provide the delimiter character, such as `,` or `|`. Defaults to `,`. For tab-delimited files, paste a tab character or use `\t`.
- `encrypted` (Boolean) Whether the files you uploaded are encrypted with Faraday's public key.
- `header_row` (String) A row of column headers. The delimiter must be the same as the `delimiter` parameter and match the data. If not provided, the first row of the CSV file will be used as the headers.
- `replace_all_with_latest_file` (Boolean) Defaults to false, which means all files are merged into the dataset. If set to true, every time the dataset is ingested, delete all previous data and replace it with only the data in the latest file. This setting only guarantees that previous data is deleted and older files are not processed; however this process may run more than once. Therefore you cannot use this functionality to ensure "exactly once' delivery of a downstream target.


<a id="nestedatt--options--hosted_csv"></a>
### Nested Schema for `options.hosted_csv`

Required:

- `upload_directory` (String) Subdirectory of uploads where files are stored and retrieved. A directory is dedicated to one or more files which ought to have the same shape and contents. One or more datasets can pull from that folder (and in different ways) and push to one or more event streams. So if you have two different types of orders from two different POS/ecommerce systems, you would put them each in separate folders. Then you would create two different datasets that would both point to an `orders` stream.

Optional:

- `delimiter` (String) Provide the delimiter character, such as `,` or `|`. Defaults to `,`. For tab-delimited files, paste a tab character or use `\t`.
- `encrypted` (Boolean) Whether the files you uploaded are encrypted with Faraday's public key.
- `header_row` (String) A row of column headers. The delimiter must be the same as the `delimiter` parameter and match the data. If not provided, the first row of the CSV file will be used as the headers.
- `replace_all_with_latest_file` (Boolean) Defaults to false, which means all files are merged into the dataset. If set to true, every time the dataset is ingested, delete all previous data and replace it with only the data in the latest file. This setting only guarantees that previous data is deleted and older files are not processed; however this process may run more than once. Therefore you cannot use this functionality to ensure "exactly once' delivery of a downstream target.

<a id="nestedatt--output_to_locations"></a>
### Nested Schema for `output_to_locations`

Optional:

- `city` (String) The city of each location.
- `geometry` (String) The geometry of each location, as GeoJSON or well-known text. Coordinates are decimal degrees in EPSG 4326 (WGS 84), written longitude first, and the geometry must be two-dimensional; a row whose geometry does not conform produces no location. Geometries may be points, lines, or areas; an area is used in full when measuring distance to a location, so distances are measured to the nearest edge. A column holding a bare coordinate pair is not a geometry. Split it into two columns and map them as `latitude` and `longitude` instead.
- `house_number_and_street` (List of String) The street address lines of each location.
- `latitude` (String) The latitude of each location, in decimal degrees, EPSG 4326 (WGS 84).
- `longitude` (String) The longitude of each location, in decimal degrees, EPSG 4326 (WGS 84).
- `name` (String) A human-readable label for each location.
- `postcode` (String) The postcode of each location.
- `properties` (Attributes List) Additional values to record on each location. Properties can be filtered on wherever an atlas' locations are used. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--output_to_locations--properties))
- `reference_key` (String) An identifier for each location from an external system. Reference keys must be unique within an atlas. Setting this enables filtering by `location_reference_keys` wherever an atlas' locations are used.
- `state` (String) The state of each location.

<a id="nestedatt--output_to_locations--properties"></a>
### Nested Schema for `output_to_locations.properties`

Required:

- `name` (String) The name this property is given on each location. `name` and `reference_key` are reserved for the location's own fields.

Optional:

- `column` (String) The source column this property's value is read from. Mutually exclusive with `value`.
- `value` (String) A constant value for this property, shared by every location. Mutually exclusive with `column`.



<a id="nestedatt--counts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `counts`

Read-Only:

- `empty_geometry` (Number) The number of rows whose geometry was read but encloses nowhere, such as an empty point. There is no place for such a row to put a location.
- `locatable` (Number) The number of rows that produced a location. Rows that could not be located are not included in the atlas.
- `oversized_geometry` (Number) The number of rows whose geometry's GeoJSON exceeds 1 MB.
- `rows` (Number) The total number of rows in the source data.
- `unreadable_geometry` (Number) The number of rows that produced no geometry to place a location from. What was wrong depends on the columns the atlas locates its rows by: a geometry that was missing or could not be read, including coordinates outside the range of longitude and latitude or in a projection other than WGS 84; a latitude or longitude that was missing or not a number, or a latitude outside ±90; or an address that was empty or could not be geocoded.


<a id="nestedatt--detected_columns"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detected_columns`

Read-Only:

- `fill_rate` (Number) Count of non-null values divided by total count of values. 0.75 means 75% of the values are not null.
- `identifier_recommendation` (List of String) A list of recommended identity set keys to map this column to. Ordered by relevance.
- `is_nullable` (Boolean)
- `name` (String) Name of the column found in the client data.
